claims.text: This trip's own telemetry establishes the deviation. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and the trace records 34.17 km against the 27.1 km booked optimal — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%, which clears both establishment tests (greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute). The rounded 34.2 km on the trip record is a convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test, but the two agree in substance, so the rider's account of a trip roughly a quarter longer than the route she has taken dozens of times is made out on the platform's own data.

The driver's PIE advisory excuses only a capped part of that excess. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative - booked optimal) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal is 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes. The remaining 2.17 km is unexplained on any clause in the policy: the driver drove 34.17 km when the shortest lawful alternative around the closure was 30.1 km, and the rider had asked him in chat to keep it short. Nothing in POL-RD-03, and no other clause on the record, licenses the excess beyond 4.90 km.

The refund is then arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run against the closure-adjusted optimal route because POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess: charged_total 43.41; recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 km + 0.28 x 40.1 min) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 39.828; refund = charged_total less recomputed_fare = 3.582, which rounds up to a payable of SGD 3.60. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND: it is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below 90% of charged_total, so neither NO_ACTION nor FULL_REFUND follows.

Nothing on this record closes off the distance refund. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so this is not an upfront-quoted trip, POL-RD-11 does not apply, and the rider is not confined to pass-through corrections: POL-RD-02 governs the remedy and the recomputation above is the figure the ruling must state.

The driver cannot move his detour onto the rider. POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation only to the extent it is attributable to a rider instruction, and there is no rider instruction here: the only route-proposing message on the log is the driver's own at 20:38:12 ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok'), and the rider's single reply, 'ok but not too long ah', is an acknowledgment carrying a limit — it comes after the choice was announced, it names no road, and it carries no waypoint_hint. POL-RD-04(a) and (c) are not met, so no distance is excluded from the excess on this ground, and the driver's own selection of ECP, MCE and the AYE beyond the closure stands unexcused.

The other advisory in the bundle excuses nothing, and its impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired: admissibility weight 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE. It describes a breakdown on the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters — intersects_route is false and the trace carries no fix inside its geometry — and it was entered by the operator rather than ingested from the LTA feed. POL-RD-03 exonerates only an advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, so the driver's CTE assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and reduces no part of the excess.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged and has shifted to the driver. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-00104, the trace's first fix at 20:35:10 matches the trip record's started_at, and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold; it is therefore for the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. The most he can do is the PIE advisory, and that is capped, so nothing outside the 4.90 km exonerated band is taken off the excess.

The trace needs no independent corroboration and is not impaired for policy purposes. It carries 283 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval with 100% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met, the deviation may be established on the trace alone, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

This case should be ruled on, not escalated. Every POL-RD-10 trigger is absent: the three artifacts carry matching trip identifiers, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, the PIE advisory is present and covers the trip window so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged by it, the computed refund is far below SGD 150, and no charge line in the fare_breakdown is unmatched. There is no reason to hold the disputed sum instead of ruling on it, and the rider asks for a monetary ruling.

No corroboration condition attaches to this rider's claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, far below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required; and in any event that factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

claims.text: The LTA DataMall collision in EV-ADVIS-00104-01 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) satisfies every limb of POL-RD-03. It names a road the booked optimal route traverses - 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Eunos Link exit', and the optimal route source on the trip record is 'PIE westbound throughout'. Its validity window, 20:02 to 21:35 on 16 July 2026, straddles the trip's 20:35:10 to 21:22:10 running time with far more than the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03 allows at each end. And the trace matches it: the vehicle leaves the PIE at the Bedok North Ave 4 exit ahead of the blocked segment and rejoins on the AYE, with derived.advisory_area recording trace_enters_area true, 24 fixes inside the advisory box and a minimum distance to it of 0 m.

The exoneration is capped as POL-RD-03 requires, and the cap does real work here: justified excess = min(measured 7.07 km, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00 = 4.90 km) = 4.90 km. The closure-adjusted optimal route is therefore 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, with duration scaled from the booked 34.0 min to 40.1 min. On this trip 4.90 km of the 7.07 km excess is exonerated because the driver correctly avoided a HIGH-severity closure on the very expressway the optimal route uses.

Once POL-RD-03 applies, POL-RD-01 requires optimal_distance_km to be measured as the adjusted optimal that clause produces, and it requires the trace figure to govern, not the rounded trip_record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 34.17 km. Against the closure-adjusted 32.00 km the excess is 2.17 km, which is 6.8% of optimal. The absolute limb (greater than 0.8 km) is met but the percentage limb (greater than 20%) fails, and POL-RD-01 requires BOTH to pass. No deviation is established, so the outcome is NO_ACTION, which on this rider-filed dispute leaves the CHARGED fare and the nil refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand (POL-GEN-03 is party-relative: the charge stays in place).

In the alternative, if the tribunal holds that some deviation survives the adjustment, POL-RD-02 run against the closure-adjusted optimal route produces at most SGD 3.60. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0 on EV-FARE-00104) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. charged_total is 43.41, so the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to 3.60 on a PARTIAL_REFUND. That is 8.3% of the charge: far short of the SGD 14.00 the rider contests and far short of the 90% share that would convert it to a FULL_REFUND.

No POL-RD-06 uplift or referral is available against this driver on this trip. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 288, so neither the three-or-more limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb with 40 or more trips is met; and the measured excess (7.07 km and 26.09%) is below both materiality gates of 8.0 km and 50%, so HALF-REFUND under POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable on its own terms. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field and cannot be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure the clause names (POL-GEN-01). The ceiling for the rider is therefore the POL-RD-02 partial at most, with no conduct referral.

Nothing is added by POL-RD-09. The fare_breakdown shows erp_gantries empty and tolls_erp 0.00, so there is no off-route gantry to correct; the airport_surcharge is 0.0 and the trip originates at Our Tampines Hub, not an airport, so no surcharge is wrongly applied; and no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record. There is accordingly no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity finding to add to whatever the distance and time arithmetic yields.

The driver discharges the POL-RD-08 burden with a specific artifact and a specific clause, not with a general complaint that traffic was bad. EV-ADVIS-00104-01 is an LTA DataMall advisory carrying an advisory_id, a named road, a validity window overlapping the trip and a geometry that touches the trace; it is invoked under POL-RD-03. That is precisely the showing POL-RD-08 requires of a driver answering an established excess.

The second advisory, EV-ADVIS-00104-02, is impaired and I disclose it: weight_multiplier 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE. Its own payload records intersects_route false because the trace never enters the CTE box between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE. The driver does not rely on it for exoneration. Its rejection is on the merits under POL-RD-03 limb (a) - the optimal route never traverses the CTE - and not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, because the advisory is present in the pool and its window covers the trip.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so the case can and should be ruled on the merits. Trip identifier TRP-00104 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 283 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not engaged and no ESCALATE under POL-RD-10(3) arises. No timestamps conflict, and the exculpatory advisory is present and in window.

The diversion was occasioned by the closure, not chosen by the driver. At 20:38:12, three minutes after the trip started and at the point the trace leaves the PIE, the driver told the rider in the app 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok'. The rider replied 'ok but not too long ah', which acknowledged the road to be taken without naming or requesting one. The detour was announced as it was taken and was a response to the advisory, which is what POL-RD-03 limb (c) contemplates.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this is a provisional automated ruling.

THE MEASUREMENTS. The GPS trace for this trip (EV-GPS-00104, weight 1.0) measures 34.17 km between pickup and dropoff. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern; the 34.2 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00104) is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. The booked optimal route was 27.1 km, so the measured excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal — above both the 20% and the 0.8 km tests, so a deviation is established under POL-RD-01.

THE CLOSURE EXPLAINS MOST OF IT. The driver's account of an accident is corroborated by the LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, weight 1.0): a HIGH-severity multi-vehicle accident on the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link exit — the expressway the booked optimal route uses ('PIE westbound throughout') — active 20:02–21:35, which covers the trip, with the trace showing the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 ahead of the blocked segment and rejoining on the AYE. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met. Exoneration is capped: justified excess = min(7.07 km, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal route is 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes.

THE REFUND. POL-RD-03 provides that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route. Run on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00104, weight 1.0; fare_model METERED, surge multiplier 1.0 read from that artifact): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 39.828. Refund = charged_total 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of the charge, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

THE DRIVER'S NO_ACTION ARGUMENT IS REJECTED. It is correct that 2.17 km (6.8%) of excess remains against the adjusted optimal, but POL-RD-01 establishes the deviation on the trip as driven against the booked optimal (7.07 km, 26.09%), and POL-RD-03 expressly refunds the excess beyond its cap under POL-RD-02 against the adjusted route. The 2.17 km the driver drove beyond what the closure justifies is the driver's own responsibility, not the rider's.

THE RIDER'S CLAIM OF ABOUT $14 IS NOT SUPPORTED. The rider is right that 34 km is far longer than her usual 27 km and that $43.41 is about $14 above her normal fare; but a documented closure justified 4.90 km of that excess, so only the excess beyond it is refunded.

OTHER CLAIMS. ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this is my ruling on trip TRP-00104 of 16 July 2026, Tampines (Our Tampines Hub) to one-north. The deviation was real, but the driver's explanation for most of it is good, so the rider gets a small refund, not the $14 she asked for.

1. The measurement (POL-RD-01). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104, weight 1.0, 283 fixes, 10-second sampling, no gaps) records 34.17 km; the booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-00104) was 27.1 km. I use the trace figure, not the rounded 34.2 km copy, because POL-RD-01 says the trace governs. The excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of the optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (over 20%, over 0.8 km), so the deviation is established. It is not MATERIAL (under 50% and under 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral follows from it.

2. The driver's partial excuse (POL-RD-03). The LTA DataMall advisory EV-ADVIS-00104-01 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) names the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos, which is the expressway the booked optimal route uses; its window 20:02-21:35 straddles the 20:35-21:22 trip; and the trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked segment and rejoins on the AYE. That satisfies POL-RD-03. The exoneration is capped: justified excess = min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes. So 4.90 km of the 7.07 km is excused; the remaining 2.17 km is not.

3. The driver's NO_ACTION submission is refused. The argument that, measured against the adjusted 32.00 km, the remaining 2.17 km is only 6.8% and so fails POL-RD-01, leaving nothing payable, is rejected. The deviation is established on the excess as driven from the booked optimal, and POL-RD-03 itself directs that the excess beyond its cap 'is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route'. To let the establishment test swallow that direction would make the cap and the adjusted-route refund dead letters. The driver is not penalised for avoiding the closure; he accounts for the 2.17 km driven beyond even the capped allowance.

4. The driver's CTE breakdown excuse fails. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired (weight_multiplier 0.25; issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED, UNVERIFIED_SOURCE), and in any case it describes the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters (intersects_route false; no fix inside its box). POL-RD-03(a) is not met, so it excuses nothing. Because it is present in the pool and its window covers the trip, its rejection is on the merits and is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation; it simply carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13. The finding does not rest on that artifact, so its discount does not lower confidence.

5. The rider's further points. The ECP/MCE/AYE route was not rider-requested: the only route proposal in the chat log (EV-CHAT-00104) is the driver's own ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok') and the rider's 'ok but not too long ah' is an acknowledgment, not an instruction with a road or waypoint, so no distance is excluded under POL-RD-04. POL-RD-11 does not apply: the fare model on EV-FARE-00104 is METERED with no quoted fare. No corroboration condition attaches to the rider: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, well below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08.

6. The money (POL-RD-02), computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00104) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. charged_total = 43.41. 8. Confidence 0.90, capped by the weight 1.0 of the artifacts that carry the decision (EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104, EV-ADVIS-00104-01). The $3.60 refund is at or below the $8.00 automatic-execution threshold and is executed on issue; fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is set to 3.60. Either party may appeal once, within 30 days, through the help channel.

POL-RD-09 finds nothing to correct: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00 and the trip does not originate at an airport, so there is no billing-integrity finding. POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10 are not engaged: the trace has 283 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0; trip id TRP-00104 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; and no timestamps conflict. The ruling rests on artifacts all at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104, EV-ADVIS-00104-01), so the confidence cap is 1.0; confidence is stated at 0.85. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue.

POL-RD-04(a) and (c) are not met, so no distance is excluded from the excess on this ground, and the driver's own selection of ECP, MCE and the AYE beyond the closure stands unexcused.

The other advisory in the bundle excuses nothing, and its impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired: admissibility weight 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE. It describes a breakdown on the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters — intersects_route is false and the trace carries no fix inside its geometry — and it was entered by the operator rather than ingested from the LTA feed. POL-RD-03 exonerates only an advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, so the driver's CTE assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and reduces no part of the excess.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged and has shifted to the driver. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-00104, the trace's first fix at 20:35:10 matches the trip record's started_at, and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold; it is therefore for the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. The most he can do is the PIE advisory, and that is capped, so nothing outside the 4.90 km exonerated band is taken off the excess.

The trace needs no independent corroboration and is not impaired for policy purposes. It carries 283 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval with 100% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met, the deviation may be established on the trace alone, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

This case should be ruled on, not escalated. Every POL-RD-10 trigger is absent: the three artifacts carry matching trip identifiers, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, the PIE advisory is present and covers the trip window so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged by it, the computed refund is far below SGD 150, and no charge line in the fare_breakdown is unmatched. There is no reason to hold the disputed sum instead of ruling on it, and the rider asks for a monetary ruling.

No corroboration condition attaches to this rider's claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, far below the four-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required; and in any event that factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

The LTA DataMall collision in EV-ADVIS-00104-01 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) satisfies every limb of POL-RD-03. It names a road the booked optimal route traverses - 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Eunos Link exit', and the optimal route source on the trip record is 'PIE westbound throughout'. Its validity window, 20:02 to 21:35 on 16 July 2026, straddles the trip's 20:35:10 to 21:22:10 running time with far more than the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03 allows at each end. And the trace matches it: the vehicle leaves the PIE at the Bedok North Ave 4 exit ahead of the blocked segment and rejoins on the AYE, with derived.advisory_area recording trace_enters_area true, 24 fixes inside the advisory box and a minimum distance to it of 0 m.

The exoneration is capped as POL-RD-03 requires, and the cap does real work here: justified excess = min(measured 7.07 km, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00 = 4.90 km) = 4.90 km. The closure-adjusted optimal route is therefore 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, with duration scaled from the booked 34.0 min to 40.1 min. On this trip 4.90 km of the 7.07 km excess is exonerated because the driver correctly avoided a HIGH-severity closure on the very expressway the optimal route uses.

Once POL-RD-03 applies, POL-RD-01 requires optimal_distance_km to be measured as the adjusted optimal that clause produces, and it requires the trace figure to govern, not the rounded trip_record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 34.17 km. Against the closure-adjusted 32.00 km the excess is 2.17 km, which is 6.8% of optimal. The absolute limb (greater than 0.8 km) is met but the percentage limb (greater than 20%) fails, and POL-RD-01 requires BOTH to pass. No deviation is established, so the outcome is NO_ACTION, which on this rider-filed dispute leaves the CHARGED fare and the nil refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand (POL-GEN-03 is party-relative: the charge stays in place).

In the alternative, if the tribunal holds that some deviation survives the adjustment, POL-RD-02 run against the closure-adjusted optimal route produces at most SGD 3.60. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0 on EV-FARE-00104) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. charged_total is 43.41, so the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to 3.60 on a PARTIAL_REFUND. That is 8.3% of the charge: far short of the SGD 14.00 the rider contests and far short of the 90% share that would convert it to a FULL_REFUND.

No POL-RD-06 uplift or referral is available against this driver on this trip. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 288, so neither the three-or-more limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb with 40 or more trips is met; and the measured excess (7.07 km and 26.09%) is below both materiality gates of 8.0 km and 50%, so HALF-REFUND under POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable on its own terms. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field and cannot be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure the clause names (POL-GEN-01). The ceiling for the rider is therefore the POL-RD-02 partial at most, with no conduct referral.

ledger.claim: Nothing is added by POL-RD-09. The fare_breakdown shows erp_gantries empty and tolls_erp 0.00, so there is no off-route gantry to correct; the airport_surcharge is 0.0 and the trip originates at Our Tampines Hub, not an airport, so no surcharge is wrongly applied; and no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record. There is accordingly no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity finding to add to whatever the distance and time arithmetic yields.

ledger.claim: The driver discharges the POL-RD-08 burden with a specific artifact and a specific clause, not with a general complaint that traffic was bad. EV-ADVIS-00104-01 is an LTA DataMall advisory carrying an advisory_id, a named road, a validity window overlapping the trip and a geometry that touches the trace; it is invoked under POL-RD-03. That is precisely the showing POL-RD-08 requires of a driver answering an established excess.

The second advisory, EV-ADVIS-00104-02, is impaired and I disclose it: weight_multiplier 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE. Its own payload records intersects_route false because the trace never enters the CTE box between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE. The driver does not rely on it for exoneration. Its rejection is on the merits under POL-RD-03 limb (a) - the optimal route never traverses the CTE - and not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, because the advisory is present in the pool and its window covers the trip.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so the case can and should be ruled on the merits. Trip identifier TRP-00104 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 283 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not engaged and no ESCALATE under POL-RD-10(3) arises. No timestamps conflict, and the exculpatory advisory is present and in window.

The diversion was occasioned by the closure, not chosen by the driver. At 20:38:12, three minutes after the trip started and at the point the trace leaves the PIE, the driver told the rider in the app 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok'. The rider replied 'ok but not too long ah', which acknowledged the road to be taken without naming or requesting one. The detour was announced as it was taken and was a response to the advisory, which is what POL-RD-03 limb (c) contemplates.
